content: The article opens with a personal reflection on how, for a disabled millennial, even ordinary activities like leaving home, going to work, socialising, or seeing others regularly can no longer be assumed. It highlights new Scope research showing that nearly half of working-age disabled people in Britain are chronically lonely, amounting to around 3 million people, and places this in the wider context of a national loneliness problem, especially among young people, while arguing that disabled people face an especially severe form of isolation.
